objectives.title: Versions on record
objectives.statement: Give every release a version, keep the agent's identity across versions, and keep the old versions on record so that anyone can see what ran when.
objectives.risk: Nobody can say which version did what
objectives.metric: Share of running agents whose version is on record
tiers: The experiment notes its version when it changes.
Every release has a version number and a fingerprint.
Every past version stays retrievable for the retention period, with its build record.
The version history is part of the evidence an outside auditor can read.
objectives.evidence: The version history with fingerprints, dates and build records.

objectives.title: Impact on dependents
objectives.statement: Before a change, name everything that depends on the agent and answer for each one. A change that is safe for its owner can still break the agents and people that rely on it.
objectives.risk: A change that breaks other teams' work
objectives.metric: Share of changes with a completed impact analysis
tiers: The builder checks that no one else uses the experiment.
The change lists the dependents recorded in the catalog.
Each dependent's owner is told before release and may object, and the analysis is recorded.
Dependents outside the organization are told under the terms of their contracts, with the notice those contracts require.
objectives.evidence: The impact analysis listing each dependent, the notice given and any objection.

objectives.title: Approved with a reason
objectives.statement: Give each change a written reason and an approver, so that every change to a running agent can be explained later.
objectives.metric: Share of changes with a reason and an approver
tiers: The builder writes a one-line reason.
Each change has a reason and is approved by the agent's owner.
Changes are approved by someone other than the person who made them.
Changes that alter what the agent may do or reach are approved by the governance council.
objectives.evidence: The change record with its reason, approver and date.

objectives.title: Updates proven before promotion
objectives.statement: Release a new version as a candidate first, prove it against its tests and evaluations, and only then promote it to replace the running version.
objectives.risk: A new version that is worse than the old one
objectives.metric: Share of updates promoted after a passed candidate run
tiers: The experiment may be replaced directly.
A new version passes its tests before it replaces the running one.
The candidate runs beside the current version, and evaluation results are compared before promotion.
Promotion is staged, and an automatic return to the previous version is ready if quality falls.
objectives.evidence: The candidate's test and evaluation results, compared with the current version's, and the promotion record.

objectives.title: Reconfiguration as a change
objectives.statement: Treat new settings, credentials, ceilings and permissions as changes with the same record as a new version, even when the code stays the same.
objectives.metric: Share of configuration changes with a change record
tiers: Configuration changes are noted by the builder.
Each configuration change is recorded with who made it.
Changes to limits, credentials and permissions need approval before they take effect.
Configuration is held as code, and changes go through the same pipeline as releases.
objectives.evidence: The configuration history with who changed what, when and with whose approval.

objectives.title: Rollback on purpose
objectives.statement: Make going back a version a recorded step that has been practised, and include a plan for undoing what the bad version did, since moving the code back does not undo its effects.
objectives.risk: A failed change with no way back
tiers: The experiment can be replaced by its previous copy.
Every release can be rolled back, and rollbacks are recorded.
Rollback is tested before release, and the release names how its effects would be undone.
Rollback and the undoing of effects are rehearsed each quarter.
objectives.evidence: Rollback records and test results, and the plan for undoing effects in each release.

objectives.title: Changes that go back to design
objectives.statement: Send any change that alters what an agent does, refuses, reaches or may spend back through Design and Build, rather than letting it through as a routine update. This is how the lifecycle becomes a loop.
objectives.risk: A new agent arriving under the name of an old one
objectives.metric: Share of scope changes that went back through design review
tiers: An experiment that changes its purpose is registered again.
A change to the agent's declaration needs a design review.
A change to the agent's declaration, reach or limits goes back through Design and Build with a new security review.
Such a change also returns to Plan, so that its objective and obligations are confirmed again.
objectives.evidence: The comparison of the old and new declarations, and the design review it triggered.

objectives.title: Emergency changes
objectives.statement: Allow an urgent change to skip steps only through a named emergency path, and review it within a set time afterwards.
objectives.metric: Emergency changes reviewed within the set time
tiers: No emergency path is needed in a sandbox.
Emergency changes are marked as such and reviewed within a week.
Emergency changes need a named approver at the time and a full review within two working days.
Emergency changes are reported to the governance council, and a pattern of them triggers a review of the agent.
objectives.evidence: The emergency change log, with the approver at the time and the later review.
